proof_logic.evidence: Independently reconstructed the Hodge-family argument in 03_gluing.tex:80-109: partial normalization gives the structure-sheaf incidence complex with cokernel H^1(Gamma) tensor O; relative duality gives the stated H_1 quotient. Equivalently the prescribed external residues on each connected nodal vertex curve have only the total-residue obstruction. This works over the full labelled product, not just its smooth-vertex locus. The quotient is trivial there, but loop reversal acts by a sign; no equivariant triviality on the graph quotient is claimed. Whitney multiplication and coefficient extraction then give the exact defect formula. Logarithmic dualizing restriction, with gluing branches counted as markings, proves kappa additivity and leg-line preservation. The boundary proof groups actual local boundary branches, uses their algebraic normal-line self-intersections and labelled multiplicities, then applies projection formula. The one-point algebraic kappa comparison uses stabilization of the old logarithmic dualizing line, adding the new section, projection/flat base change and the stated binomial calculation. The tail proof annihilates the comparison-divisor ideal by restriction to compact rational factors; passing to polynomials or graded series is therefore justified and retains the new-psi sum. These algebraic inputs support the cited one-point KMZ push-pull recursion for every a_i>=0. The singleton/insertion recursion counts permutations, and the inverse proof's formal identity sum (1-exp(-z))^k/k=z leaves only singleton resulting blocks. Labelled block-size counting then produces exactly psi_new(1-exp(-s psi_new)). No circular use, unsupported class-lift inference or unresolved essential step remains.

uniformity.evidence: All full-section exports are exact finite-genus Chow or formal graded identities. The fixed-(g,n) graph set is finite, all boundary/vertex exponentials are truncated by codimension, and the fractions in K_a are formal divisible series rather than inverse classes or analytic integrals. The finite partition/cycle formulas have fixed m; their signed generating-series proof is coefficientwise formal. In the exponential specialization each new factor has degree at least two, so forgetting m points leaves codimension at least m and terms m>3g-3+n vanish. This cutoff uses the actual degree-two factor, not merely the tail lemma's weaker degree-one assumption. The tail exponential is also a graded identity, with the retained -c sum_new psi term. The roadmap, 2.1 parameter table and final paragraph of 2.4 explicitly distinguish these finite-genus statements from the later uniform bounds needed for sums whose graph or marking data grow with genus. No unproved interchange of a genus limit with a growing sum, integral or coefficient extraction is claimed.
